subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Propeller: Spinning Airfoil in Disguise
description: A fast breakdown of The Propeller: Spinning Airfoil in Disguise for builders.

hook.text: A propeller is not a fan. It's a rotating wing. Each blade is an airfoil generating forward thrust.

buildup.text: Propeller blades are twisted from root to tip. The twist compensates for the difference in speed along the blade's length.

discovery.text: The tip moves much faster than the hub. Without the twist, the tip would stall while the hub produces no thrust.

twist.text: Variable-pitch propellers adjust blade angle in flight. They act like gear shifts — fine pitch for takeoff, coarse for cruise.

climax.text: Modern turboprops combine jet engines with propellers. They're more fuel-efficient than pure jets at speeds below 450 mph.

punchline.text: Twist the blade. Spin it fast. A rotating wing pulls you forward.

quiz.question: Why are propeller blades twisted from root to tip?
options: The twist makes the propeller quieter by reducing tip noise
It compensates for speed differences along the blade's length to prevent stalling
Twisted blades are structurally stronger against centrifugal forces
